text:
The gain errors point to a common-mode gain loss in the op-amp, not an input-resistor error. Both measured gains are 0.801× their ideal values (Rf/R1 and Rf/R2), so the error doesn't depend on which input is driven. That pattern indicates finite, too-low open-loop gain, roughly A ≈ 4. The bandwidth and power are still in spec, so the fault is most likely in the gain-setting output stage rather than in the input network or the bias.

The output-stage pFET M7 is the most likely culprit. Its short L = 0.43 µm and its gm·ro product set the second-stage gain, so a corrupted size there would cut the loop gain without affecting power or bandwidth much. M8, the output current sink, and the first-stage pair M1/M2 are the next candidates.
